title: Scale Calculator
desc: Scale calculator determines the size of scaled/real structures for a given scale or evaluates the scale between two objects.

c: conversion_type_VS == 1 and length_conversion_options_VS == 0 and length_scaled_input == 0.05 and length_real_input == 5000
Onim Example 1: Map scale – What is the scale factor of a map where 5 cm represents 5 km in real life?
conversion_type_VS == 2 and area_conversion_options_VS == 2 and scale_factor_form_VS == 0 and scale_ratio_nominator == 1 and scale_ratio_denominator == 100 and area_scaled_input == 0.0025
Onim Example 2: Floor plan – What is the real area of a room that measures 25 cm² on a 1:100 scale plan?
conversion_type_VS == 3 and volume_conversion_options_VS == 2 and scale_factor_form_VS == 0 and scale_ratio_nominator == 1 and scale_ratio_denominator == 50 and volume_scaled_input == 0.02
Onim Example 3: Scale model – What is the real volume of a building if a 1:50 scale model has a volume of 0.02 m³?
We use e-notation to display the scale factor (e.g., 3e-8 = 3·10-8).
conversion_type_VS == 1 and length_conversion_options_VS == 0 and length_scaled_input == 0.05 and length_real_input == 5000
How the result is calculated: Convert lengths to the same units. Divide the scaled length by the real length to find the scale factor: Scale factor = 5 cm / 500,000 cm = 1:100,000
conversion_type_VS == 2 and area_conversion_options_VS == 2 and scale_factor_form_VS == 0 and scale_ratio_nominator == 1 and scale_ratio_denominator == 100 and area_scaled_input == 0.0025

How the result is calculated: Identify the scale factor: 1:100. Square it to account for area scaling: Area factor = 100² = 10,000 Multiply the scaled area by the area factor to find the real area: Real area = 25 cm² × 10,000 = 250,000 cm² = 25 m²
conversion_type_VS == 3 and volume_conversion_options_VS == 2 and scale_factor_form_VS == 0 and scale_ratio_nominator == 1 and scale_ratio_denominator == 50 and volume_scaled_input == 0.02

How the result is calculated: Identify the scale factor: 1:50 Cube it to account for volume scaling: Volume factor = 50³ = 125,000 Multiply the model’s volume by the volume factor to find the real volume: Real volume = 0.02 m³ × 125,000 = 2,500 m³
Check our examples: • Example 1 ⧉ – Map scale (length) • Example 2 ⧉ – Floor plan (area) • Example 3 ⧉ – Scale model (volume)
